The Squirrel and the Bridge

Bridges don't fail where the biggest rocks are placed. They fail where the small gaps are ignored.

EssayDecember 9, 20252 min read
#WorkingPrinciples#AttentiontoDetail

Armies are moving massive stones. The vision is bold. The structure is ambitious. In the middle of all this, a small squirrel keeps carrying tiny pebbles, one at a time. Ever wondered what the squirrel is doing here?

I used to open my presentations with this image. I'd tell them: you're doing the hard, visible work, designing complex systems. I'm not here to redesign the bridge or challenge the vision. I'm here to focus on the gaps.

Because bridges don't fail where the biggest rocks are placed. They fail where the small gaps are ignored. Those gaps look minor, until stress hits, until compliance is tested, until what looked right on paper meets the reality of the field.

In high-stakes environments, this mindset isn't optional. It's the difference between a system that appears strong and one that actually holds.

I've chosen to do the work that protects what others build. To strengthen systems before they're tested. One pebble at a time.

Do you focus on the big rocks, or the gaps?
